data.title: Around 600% jump in 5 years: Citi maintains 'buy' on Maharatna defence PSU HAL for up to 28% - Check target, rationale
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL) shares have recently faced selling pressure, with the Maharatna defence public sector undertaking (PSU) stock declining 3.5% in one week, 1% in one month and 3% in three months. However, the stock remained in positive territory over longer periods, gaining 4% in six months and 1% in one year. It also delivered multibagger returns of around 600% over five years.

In the previous trading session, HAL shares fell 0.7% to close at Rs.4,809.80. Despite the recent weakness, international brokerage Citi maintained its bullish stance on the defence major, retaining its 'Buy' rating and target price of Rs.6,175 per share. The target indicated an upside potential of around 28% from the previous close.

Citi said HAL's Q2 revenue was in line with its estimates, although EBITDA missed expectations due to weaker gross margins. The brokerage added that the company's engines, helicopters and repair work helped offset the delayed Mk1A ramp-up. HAL's inventory also increased 39% year-on-year (YoY), signalling rising preparedness for execution, according to the report.

The Maharatna central public sector enterprise reported its financial results for the July-September quarter during market hours on Thursday.

HAL posted a 16% YoY increase in consolidated profit after tax (PAT) to Rs.1,935.64 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs.1,669.05 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.

The defence major's revenue from operations rose nearly 15% YoY to Rs.7,613.25 crore in Q2 FY27, against Rs.6,628.61 crore reported in the year-ago period. Expenses, meanwhile, increased around 16% YoY to Rs.6,132 crore during the quarter under review.

While revenue growth remained in line with Citi's estimates, the brokerage flagged weaker gross margins as the reason for the EBITDA shortfall. The company's engines, helicopters and repair activities provided support amid delays in the Tejas Mk1A delivery ramp-up.

Analysts view rising Tejas Mk1A output, improving execution capacity, government support and management guidance as positive for HAL's earnings outlook.

Retaining its 'Buy' rating on HAL, Citi maintained its target price at Rs.6,175 per share, indicating a 28% upside from the previous close. The brokerage said the Tejas Mk1A delivery ramp-up and improving execution readiness supported the company's medium-term growth prospects.

HAL's management has guided for FY27 revenue growth of 10-12% and an EBITDA margin of 30-31%, which Citi said remained supportive of the outlook.

The brokerage also highlighted that higher inventory and institutional backing for resolving Mk1A bottlenecks strengthened delivery visibility for the company. HAL's inventory rose 39% YoY, pointing to increased preparedness to execute orders as production and deliveries improve.

HAL's Tejas Mk1A is an upgraded version of the indigenous Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas, developed for the Indian Air Force (IAF). It features improvements in radar, electronic warfare, weapons and maintainability, making the programme an important part of the company's growth and execution outlook.

data.title: Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles Appoints Martin Pohanka As Head Of Design
data.description:
Pohanka previously held senior roles at Audi, Porsche and Jaguar Land Rover

Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles (VWCV) has appointed Martin Pohanka as Head of Design, placing him in charge of the brand’s overall design function.

Pohanka has been with VWCV since 2017 and most recently served as Head of Design Creation, overseeing interior, exterior, UI/UX and colour and trim. He will succeed in the role with extensive experience across the automotive industry, having previously held design positions at Audi, Porsche and Jaguar Land Rover.

He began his career in 1997 as a freelance industrial designer and joined Audi in 1998. He moved to Porsche in 2001, working across interior and advanced design, before joining Jaguar Land Rover in 2015 as Chief Designer of Interior Creation.

At VWCV, Pohanka initially led interior design before taking charge of Design Creation in 2023. His work has contributed to the design of models including the Multivan, ID. Buzz, latest Transporter generation and Amarok. His earlier work includes the Porsche 911, Boxster and Macan, as well as the Land Rover Defender and Range Rover.

data.title: Puneet Anand Exits Hyundai Motor India After Nearly 29 Years
data.description:
Anand, who served as AVP and Vertical Head – Corporate Affairs, Corporate Communication & Social, was associated with Hyundai Motor India for 28 years, 10 months and six days

Puneet Anand, AVP and Vertical Head - Corporate Affairs, Corporate Communication & Social at Hyundai Motor India, has announced his exit from the company after a tenure of 28 years, 10 months and six days.

Announcing his departure through a LinkedIn post, Anand said he would be taking time to reflect and recharge before moving on to his next chapter.

Anand's nearly three-decade association with Hyundai saw him take up responsibilities across several functions, including Customer Care and CRM, Marketing and Sales, Corporate Communication, Corporate Affairs and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR). His roles also involved brand-building initiatives, marketing innovations and public policy engagement.

During his tenure, Anand witnessed and contributed to several important developments in Hyundai's India operations. These included the launch of the Santro, the establishment of the company's second manufacturing plant in Chennai, its five-millionth and 10-millionth vehicle rollouts, and the introduction of the Creta, which became one of Hyundai's key models in the Indian SUV market.

He was also associated with Hyundai's acquisition and inauguration of its third manufacturing facility in Talegaon, Maharashtra.

Anand also highlighted his association with Hyundai Motor Company's headquarters in South Korea, having travelled to Seoul more than 26 times during his career. He completed his postgraduate studies in South Korea, an experience he credited with contributing significantly to his professional growth.

Reflecting on his departure, Anand thanked the company's leadership, colleagues, dealers, suppliers and business partners for their support throughout his career. He said the relationships he built and the teams he worked with remained his most valued achievements. He did not disclose details of his next professional assignment.

data.title: Puneet Anand Bids Farewell To Hyundai Motor India After 28 Years
data.description:
Anand's tenure at the automaker spanned customer relations, marketing, corporate communications, public policy and social initiatives

Puneet Anand, Associate Vice-President and Vertical Head – Corporate Affairs, Corporate Communications and Social Initiatives at Hyundai Motor India, has exited the automaker after nearly 29 years with the company.Anand announced his departure in an emotional LinkedIn post, reflecting on his 28 years, 10 months and six days with Hyundai. Describing the company as his second home, he said the organisation had shaped his professional journey and given him the opportunity to contribute to its growth in India from its early days.

During his tenure, Anand worked across several functions, including Customer Care and Customer Relationship Management (CRM), Marketing and Sales, Corporate Communications, Corporate Affairs and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR).His responsibilities included initiatives to enhance customer experience, support sales and marketing growth, shape the company's communications strategy, strengthen the Hyundai brand through marketing innovations, develop public policy narratives and lead social initiatives.

Reflecting on his career, Anand said each role had challenged him and contributed to his professional development. He also highlighted his association with Hyundai Motor Company's global operations in South Korea, having travelled to Seoul more than 26 times during his tenure.Anand further described completing his postgraduate studies in South Korea as a significant milestone in his association with the company's global parent.

Before joining Hyundai Motor India in January 1998, Anand spent two years with Mahindra & Mahindra. His departure marks the end of a career spanning nearly three decades at the automaker, during which he held responsibilities across customer relations, marketing, communications, corporate affairs and social initiatives.

data.title: Filatex India Q2 Revenue Rises 21% To Rs 1,304 Cr, PAT Up 12%
data.description:
Polyester yarn manufacturer reports Q2FY27 Ebitda of Rs 91.03 crore and net profit of Rs 53.48 crore

Filatex India reported a 21.22 per cent year-on-year increase in standalone revenue from operations to Rs 1,304.19 crore for the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 1,075.93 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, supported by steady business momentum and improving downstream demand.

The company's Ebitda increased 2.36 per cent year-on-year to Rs 91.03 crore in Q2FY27, against Rs 88.93 crore in Q2FY26. However, Ebitda margin declined to 6.98 per cent from 8.27 per cent a year earlier, reflecting pressure from elevated raw material prices. Profit after tax (PAT) rose 12.40 per cent to Rs 53.48 crore, compared with Rs 47.58 crore in the year-ago quarter.

On a sequential basis, revenue increased 13.87 per cent from Rs 1,145.30 crore in Q1FY27, while Ebitda grew 16.82 per cent from Rs 77.92 crore. PAT registered an 8.83 per cent quarter-on-quarter increase from Rs 49.14 crore.

The company's performance comes amid elevated input costs and geopolitical uncertainties in West Asia. However, downstream demand began recovering during the quarter as the cautious, need-based purchasing behaviour witnessed earlier in the year gradually eased.

H1FY27 Revenue Crosses Rs 2,449 Crore

For the six months ended September 30, 2026, Filatex India reported revenue from operations of Rs 2,449.49 crore, up from Rs 2,125.33 crore in H1FY26.

Ebitda for the first half stood at Rs 168.95 crore, compared with Rs 166.69 crore in the corresponding period last year. Ebitda margin was 6.90 per cent, against 7.84 per cent in H1FY26. PAT increased to Rs 102.62 crore from Rs 88.32 crore, registering growth of approximately 16.2 per cent.

Production during Q2FY27 stood at 94,763 metric tonnes (MT), down 5.21 per cent from 99,974 MT in Q2FY26. Sales volume declined 8.28 per cent year-on-year to 92,998 MT from 1,01,391 MT.

Sequentially, production increased 12.71 per cent from 84,076 MT in Q1FY27, while sales volume grew 3.36 per cent from 89,972 MT.

Rs 300 Crore Textile Recycling Project Nears Commissioning

Filatex India continued to advance its strategic investments in textile-to-textile recycling, polyester filament yarn capacity expansion and renewable energy during the quarter.

The company's Rs 300 crore textile-to-textile recycling project, with an installed capacity of 26,750 tonnes per annum (TPA), being developed through its wholly owned subsidiary Ecosis Limited, has reached the final stage of execution. Commissioning is expected in Q3FY27.

During September 2026, Filatex further invested Rs 20 crore in Ecosis Limited through a rights issue to support the project. The company said the project's fundamentals remained unchanged.

The recycling initiative is a key component of Filatex's strategy to strengthen its presence in high-value recycled polyester yarn and support the textile industry's transition towards more sustainable manufacturing practices.

Polyester Yarn Capacity Expansion To Be Completed By November

Alongside recycling, the company is progressing with its Rs 235 crore brownfield polyester filament yarn (PFY) capacity expansion.

The project will add approximately 55,000 TPA of capacity, primarily across partially oriented yarn (POY), fully drawn yarn (FDY) and draw textured yarn (DTY). A portion of the expanded capacity has already been commissioned, while the remaining capacity is expected to become operational by the end of November 2026.

The expansion is expected to support product mix improvement and strengthen Filatex's manufacturing capabilities across polyester filament yarn categories.

Renewable Energy Share Targeted To Reach 55 per cent

Filatex is also advancing its renewable energy transition through power sourcing arrangements involving hybrid wind-solar and solar projects.

The projects are expected to be commissioned by January 2027. Following their implementation, the company's share of renewable power in its overall energy consumption is expected to increase from approximately 26 per cent to 55 per cent.

The initiative forms part of the company's broader sustainability strategy, which focuses on cleaner energy sourcing alongside investments in recycling and high-value yarn manufacturing.

Global Brand Partnerships Support Recycled Yarn Push

Filatex continued trials of recycled polyester yarn under memoranda of understanding (MoUs) signed with American & Efird Global, LLC and Decathlon during Q2FY27.

The trials are being conducted for thread manufacturing and other applications. The company also said that approvals from several other global brands were at an advanced stage, indicating growing market interest in its recycled yarn platform.

These partnerships are expected to support the commercial development of its textile-to-textile recycling business and strengthen its engagement with global brands seeking recycled materials for their manufacturing and product portfolios.

Downstream Demand Recovery And Industry Developments

On the industry front, Filatex said downstream demand began recovering during the quarter as cautious purchasing patterns gradually eased. However, raw material prices remained elevated amid continued geopolitical tensions in West Asia. The company also highlighted developments in domestic purified terephthalic acid (PTA) capacity, which could progressively reduce India's dependence on imports.

GAIL's 1.25 million tonnes per annum Mangalore plant has been commissioned, while Indian Oil Corporation's (IOCL) 1.2 million tonnes per annum Paradip facility is nearing completion. Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) also has a planned 3 million tonnes per annum capacity addition.

According to Filatex, these developments are expected to strengthen domestic PTA availability and make recent supply disruptions transitional rather than structural.

On the trade front, the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA) moved to the signing stage in September 2026, with entry into force expected in early 2027. The company also cited India's competitive 10 per cent US tariff position as a factor supporting its long-term export competitiveness.

Chairman Highlights Execution And Cost Discipline

Commenting on the performance, Madhu Sudhan Bhageria, Chairman and Managing Director, Filatex India, said Q2FY27 was a quarter of steady execution for the company, with revenue reaching Rs 1,304.19 crore, Ebitda at Rs 91.03 crore and PAT at Rs 53.48 crore.

He said, "Q2FY27 was a quarter of steady execution for Filatex. We reported revenue of Rs 1,304.19 crore, Ebitda of Rs 91.03 crore and PAT of Rs 53.48 crore, taking H1FY27 revenue to Rs 2,449.49 crore and PAT to Rs 102.62 crore. Our integrated operations and disciplined cost management helped us protect profitability in a volatile raw material environment.

"During the quarter, raw material prices remained elevated amid continued geopolitical tensions in West Asia, while downstream demand started recovering as the cautious, need-based buying seen earlier in the year gradually eased. We continued to align production closely with demand, supported by calibrated inventory levels and disciplined sourcing, which positions us well to benefit from the improving demand environment.

"Our recycling, capacity expansion and renewable energy projects are progressing well, with the recycling and PFY expansion projects expected to be commissioned in Q3FY27, and trials of our recycled yarn with global brands are ongoing. With our scale, integrated manufacturing capabilities and early leadership in textile-to-textile recycling, we believe Filatex is well positioned for sustainable long-term growth."

With its recycling and capacity expansion projects approaching commissioning and renewable energy initiatives progressing, Filatex is looking to strengthen its manufacturing scale, improve its product mix and expand its sustainable polyester yarn portfolio. The coming quarters will be important in determining how effectively these investments translate into higher-value production, operational efficiencies and long-term business growth.

data.title: Waaree’s US Trade Disclosures Put India’s Solar Export Strategy Under Pressure
data.description:
The solar manufacturer's acknowledgement of shipment-origin reporting errors comes amid separate US customs action, raising concerns over trade compliance, export exposure and India's access to a key clean-energy market

Waaree Energies' disclosure of incorrectly classified solar imports from Vietnam and Malaysia has intensified scrutiny of India's solar trade with the United States, with the issue emerging as a potential risk for exporters navigating increasingly stringent trade regulations. The company acknowledged before the US International Trade Commission (USITC) that certain imports of solar cells and modules from Vietnam and Malaysia had inadvertently been reported as originating in India between 2021 and 2026. The disclosure came as part of a wider US investigation into solar imports from India, Indonesia and Laos.

The development is significant for India's solar manufacturing sector, which is increasingly looking towards overseas markets to absorb expanding domestic production capacity. It also highlights how discrepancies in supply-chain documentation can translate into trade disputes, potential duty liabilities and changes in export strategies.

Origin Reporting Keeps India In Trade Probe

The USITC examined whether imports from the three countries crossed the 3 per cent threshold under US trade law, below which imports are generally considered negligible for such investigations. Waaree and Mundra Solar had argued that removing incorrectly classified shipments from the import data would bring India's share below this threshold, potentially excluding the country from the proceedings. However, after reviewing corrected import figures and customs records, the commission concluded that India's share remained above the prescribed limit.

On 14 October 2026, the USITC determined that imports of crystalline silicon photovoltaic cells, whether or not assembled into modules, from India, Indonesia and Laos had materially injured the US solar manufacturing industry. The development comes alongside a separate enforcement proceeding by US Customs and Border Protection (CBP), which upheld an adverse duty-evasion determination on 29 October 2026 concerning a limited set of historical shipments. Waaree disclosed the customs decision to stock exchanges on 2 November 2026 and said it was evaluating legal remedies, including judicial review before the US Court of International Trade.

Export Exposure Drives Order Book Reset

The trade dispute has also begun influencing Waaree's commercial strategy. As of 30 September 2026, the company had removed more than 3 gigawatts (GW) of export contracts from its active reported order book amid growing uncertainty over US trade measures. Following the rationalisation, Waaree's total order book stood at approximately Rs 59,200 crore, representing 25.6 GW of capacity. Domestic orders accounted for 48.4 per cent, while its US manufacturing operations in Texas contributed 43.8 per cent. Direct exports from India made up the remaining 7.8 per cent, down from 24 per cent in the preceding quarter.

For the Indian solar industry, the case highlights the growing importance of supply-chain transparency and regulatory compliance as manufacturers expand their international footprint. Industry observers see localisation, stronger supplier verification and traceable component sourcing as increasingly important to maintaining competitiveness in global markets.

With the US remaining a significant destination for Indian solar manufacturers, the outcome of ongoing trade proceedings could influence investment decisions, export commitments and the economics of overseas expansion.

data.title: Hard Reset
data.description:
For three decades, Jensen Huang was Nvidia. Now the world’s most valuable AI bet must learn to live without him.

When Nasdaq opened on Thursday, November 12, it was 8 pm in India. Investors who had spent a few days buying the dip were watching one ticker. Nvidia, the company that supplies the picks and shovels of the AI gold rush, had just said that Jensen Huang had resigned as president, chief executive officer and board member, effective immediately.

There was no farewell and no explanation. The board’s only comment on Huang in their statement: “Jensen’s contributions to Nvidia are profound.”

Boy From the Back Room

The ending looks quite strange against the beginning. Huang, 63, was a busboy, dishwasher and waiter at Denny’s as a teenager. In 1992, he and two Sun Microsystems engineers sketched out Nvidia in a San Jose Denny’s, staying so long that the staff moved them to a back room. The first product failed, the second was canceled, and the third, the Riva 128, arrived as the money ran out.

It survived and then it conquered. Nvidia went public in 1999 at USD 12 a share. On May 30, 2023, the company hit USD 1 trillion market cap. Huang became a central figure of the AI boom, a man in a black leather jacket whom Larry Ellison joked he and Elon Musk were “begging” for GPUs.

In 2024, onstage at Stanford, he offered students a very strange blessing. “I wish upon you ample doses of pain and suffering,” he said.

Five Days in November

And a pain did arrive seemingly fast. Nvidia’s market value had already slid from roughly USD 5.78 trillion on October 6 to USD 4.51 trillion by November 6, about USD 1.27 trillion, when the board seemingly started an investigation into Huang on November 8.

US intelligence agencies reportedly found that Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, which bought billions of dollars of Nvidia chips, passed information to China. Huang admitted an affair in an email to employees (without mentioning any name). The New York Times then reported a second affair, with an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him, and Reuters later reported a third relationship. These remain reports, and the board said it had no reason to believe national security had been compromised.

On Sunday, Huang wrote to his employees. “There is no excuse for what I did,” he said. On Monday, nearly USD 192 billion vanished from Nvidia’s value while much of Wall Street rallied. When the Wall Street Journal reported, the board was preparing to remove him, the shares fell more than 8 per cent after hours.

Then came Thursday. Nvidia had closed Wednesday at USD 173.73 and opened at USD 151.00. It sank as much as 14 per cent, nearly USD 600 billion at the low, before closing about 4 per cent lower, according to Vested Finance data.

The Man Nobody Planned Without

Huang ran Nvidia with roughly 60 direct reports, and the company seemingly did not have a succession plan. Gartner, in a note published the day he resigned, said, “Huang’s departure leaves a much larger operational void than a typical large technology company’s CEO transition.”

Ganesh S. Padmanabhan of recruiter CIEL HR had a gentler reading. “I won’t say it’s unusual (for Nvidia to not have a succession plan). It all depends on context,” he says, seeing interim CEO Colette Kress and the open search as succession’s first phase at work.

The clock is another matter. At a typical company, finding a new chief takes anywhere between six to nine months, followed by a three to six months of transition. For example, look at TCS, the outgoing Rajesh Gopinathan, a few years ago, stayed for six months for the transition, Padmanabhan explains.

Nvidia, though, is a different animal. “This is an extraordinary scenario,” he says.

Markets will not wait politely. Anyone watching Nvidia, investors above all, wants a credible name in the chair to steady a stock that fell as much as 14 per cent in a day. Padmanabhan agrees on the stakes. “Having a very credible face is in my view, very important for Nvidia to continue being one of the most valued organisations in the world.”

US President Donald Trump has, meanwhile, pushed Tim Cook for the role: “A Legend to replace a Legend,” he posted on social media.

Yet no one person, Padmanabhan suggests, can fill Huang’s shoes. Huang was holding too many offices. “He was leading strategy, technology thought process, held key customer relationships.” Boards, he says “don’t make the mistake of finding someone to replicate the past or replace the past.”

“There is a possibility that multiple people may have to hold the office both combining existing internal as well as external resources who will come in,” Padmanabhan adds.

For now, the machine runs on. “We do not expect any impact to Nvidia’s ability to execute and deliver against 2027 and 2028 products,” Gartner wrote in its note. The danger is further out. “The risk becomes more significant in 2029 and beyond,” it added.

Others in the field are already looking past the upheaval. Krishna Rangasayee, Founder and CEO at SiMa.ai, a chipmaker that recently raised USD 150 million in Series C financing at a USD 1.45 billion valuation to build hardware for physical AI, the very field Gartner warns could be first to feel a slowdown in Nvidia’s vision, offers a pragmatic farewell. “The Nvidia board had to make the decision it did, and the AI industry lost a leader. But the industry will move forward, and nothing changes for us. In terms of Physical AI, the market is ready for prime time, and we are leading the industry with our technology; we remain focused on winning and delighting customers,” he says.

What Huang’s Exit Means for India

India’s AI dreams are being poured in concrete and cooled by the gigawatt: “AI factories” from Reliance, Tata, Yotta and L&T, each a wager that the world’s best chips will keep arriving. Huang’s exit perhaps does not break that bet. It does ask who is still standing behind it.

Gaurav Vasu, CEO at UnearthInsight, sees a split. Reliance and Tata have stronger funding support, and L&T has an order from Together AI. Yotta is the one to watch. It is “more exposed,” he tells BW Businessworld, because Nvidia is both its technology supplier and a major buyer of its capacity.

His check is simple, “The real test is whether financing is closed, GPUs are delivered and the capacity starts generating revenue, rather than the gigawatt-scale commitments being announced.”

Yotta and few other players in the market did not provide a comment on the potential implications when contacted by BW Businessworld.

The harder question is who bankrolls the next wave. Nvidia had grown used to financing its own customers, and Vasu sees that tap tightening now. “We expect tighter terms and longer approval timelines for new deals,” he says.

“Kress had already challenged some of the riskier financing arrangements. The proposed USD 500 billion financing platform was struggling to close transactions even before Huang’s exit.” He expects “selective postponements between January and June 2027”.

India’s IT majors, in contrast, can breathe. “The revenue impact is likely to be very limited or negligible,” Vasu says of TCS, Infosys, Wipro and HCLTech. TCS carries extra infrastructure exposure through HyperVault, and Infosys and Wipro could see slower deployment and joint-selling. But these are institutional ties, and the disclosures he reviewed give “no basis to assume that these partnerships depend on Huang’s personal backing.”

Nvidia itself has not weighed in. BW Businessworld reached out to the company to seek clarification on whether Huang’s exit is expected to have implications on India. There was no response at the time of publication.

India’s Dip Buyers

While boardrooms braced, Indian retail investors did the opposite: they bought. “Indian investors have largely approached Nvidia’s recent volatility as a buying opportunity rather than stepping away from the stock,” says Viram Shah, CEO at Vested Finance. The numbers recorded on Vested’s platform suggest so. Buying dominated selling in at least eight of the last ten sessions, at about 70 per cent of activity, and above 80 per cent on November 10 and 11. Shah is careful to add that order activity is not net capital flow.

His read is that investors are confident, but he also has a warning. When so much rides on one leader, he says, markets usually mark down a company’s value until it is clear who will take over and that the business will carry on. For first-time global investors, the lesson is that “leadership-related risks can affect even established companies with strong underlying businesses.”

“The lesson is that diversification should extend beyond individual stocks to different sectors and investment strategies,” he adds.

The Test Ahead

The first exam comes Tuesday, November 17 (early hours of November 18 IST), when Nvidia reports third-quarter fiscal 2027 results, five days after Huang’s exit. Kress, who joined in 2013, says she is committed to building on “the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years.”

The investigation’s findings have not been released. But the emperor has left the palace and the empire keeps running on his foundations. The real verdict will come when Nvidia can prove it can invent without him.

data.title: China, US discuss tariffs, farm trade ahead of Xi-Trump meeting
data.description:
China and the United States discussed tariff cuts, agricultural trade and other issues at their first trade council meeting on Friday, China's Commerce Ministry said on Saturday, days ahead of an expected leaders' meeting in Shenzhen next week.

"The two sides held candid, in-depth and constructive exchanges on implementing the outcomes of previous China-US economic and trade talks, including tariffs, a reciprocal '$30 billion-for-$30 billion' tariff-cut arrangement, agricultural trade and other issues of mutual concern," the ministry said.

It did not say whether any agreements were reached. Both sides will continue using the council to address trade concerns, expand cooperation and reduce outstanding issues, the ministry added.

Following a September summit between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump in Washington, the two sides proposed a $60 billion package of reciprocal tariff cuts, including roughly $17 billion worth of US farm goods that China imported in 2024, but the plan has yet to be finalised.

Chinese purchases of US farm goods other than soybeans are on track to hit a seven-year low this year, despite an agreement to buy $17 billion annually through 2028, a Reuters analysis of customs data showed earlier this month, underscoring persistent uncertainty over the deal.

Beijing has repeatedly urged Washington to implement the $60 billion tariff-reduction deal, calling it a prerequisite for increasing purchases of US farm goods.

The White House said Trump will meet Xi on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen.

data.title: Modi summons telecom secretary over website takedowns, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • Government probes intensifying on why fake court orders led to takedowns
  • Telecom secretary to cut short trip to appear in person at Modi's office
  • Telecoms ministry has begun internal inquiry, police seek records
  • Fake orders removed from government website on Saturday

By Aftab Ahmed, Munsif Vengattil and Aditya Kalra

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's office summoned the telecommunications secretary on Saturday to explain how officials ordered the takedown of more than 100 websites based on court orders that Reuters revealed were fake, two government sources said.

The intervention from Modi's office signals intensifying scrutiny after Reuters revealed on Wednesday that telecom officials directed internet providers to block 129 illegal betting websites based on fake High Court orders which were emailed to officials by people posing as lawyers.

While online betting is illegal in India, the case has raised concerns that a lack of safeguards in India's content-takedown system could allow falsified court documents to be used to block legitimate websites.

The findings have triggered one criminal investigation by state police against unknown persons for forgery and cheating.

Modi's office summoned Telecom Secretary Amit Agrawal to appear and explain the lapse, cutting short Agrawal's trip to another state, said the two government officials with knowledge of the matter.

Agrawal is the most senior bureaucrat in the telecommunications ministry, which oversees everyone from big telecom operators to internet providers.

"The action taken by the Department of Telecommunications against betting accounts was carried out through the relevant field officers," said one of the people.

Agrawal and his ministry did not respond to Reuters queries, and neither did Modi's office.

Court precedents generated using AI have caused concerns among judges the world over. India's Supreme Court in July set aside a tribunal's orders that relied on non-existent judgments, and a US judge recently disqualified lawyers over use of fabricated legal citations.

On Friday, Reuters reported that the telecoms ministry had initiated an internal investigation into the alleged fraud, while police have sought ministry records as part of a criminal investigation.

The two state court orders Reuters revealed were fake, based on comments from police and the court registry, contained fabricated court logos and seals, ​as well as a fake QR code.

They were for months available publicly on the Department of Telecommunications' website, along with correspondence that showed government officials ordering internet providers to remove the websites.

On Saturday, one of the fake court orders was still accessible on the government's website, while one had been removed.

data.title: Twenty One Capital CEO Says ‘A Balance Sheet Is Not A Business’ After $1 Billion Bitcoin-Driven Gain
data.description:
Key points:
  • Twenty One Capital CEO Raphael Zagury also said he did not want the company’s success to rest on predicting markets.
  • Zagury also said the company could buy back its own stock, but no buyback has been announced yet.
  • The company reported net income of $1.087 billion for its third quarter which ended on September 30.

Twenty One Capital (XXI) CEO Raphael Zagury told shareholders that the company needed to build a real business around its Bitcoin (BTC) holdings, adding that 'Bitcoin remains our benchmark.' The company’s profit from Bitcoin alone stood at a little over $1 billion in its third quarter.

In a shareholder letter, Zagury explained that “A balance sheet is not a business. It is our starting point.” The company reported net income of $1.087 billion for the quarter that ended on September 30. Zagury said that result was “primarily driven by a $1.093 billion fair-value gain” on its Bitcoin, “rather than operating cash flow.”

“We welcome Bitcoin’s appreciation. But gains from an asset we own are not the same as earnings from businesses we operate,” he wrote, adding that, “Building the latter is our job.”

XXI stock was down over 1% during overnight trading. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around XXI remained in the ‘bullish’ zone, while chatter around it shifted to ‘normal’ from ‘low’ levels over the past day.

Bitcoin As The Benchmark

Twenty One ended the September quarter with 43,514 BTC, valued at about $83,700 per coin, and $102.8 million in cash. It had $486.5 million in convertible notes outstanding, secured by about 16,116 BTC. Zagury said Bitcoin was the bar any new investment had to clear.

Any capital the company deployed “should justify the risk, complexity, and opportunity cost of not simply owning more Bitcoin,” he wrote. The company was looking at deals in mining, lending and energy, according to the letter. Zagury said it has already walked away from some of them and expected to walk away from more.

Bitcoin’s price was trading at $67,094, down over 2% in the last 24 hours. On Stocktwits, Bitcoin was one of the top trending tickers among cryptocurrencies at the time of writing.

Retail sentiment around BTCnearly 70% remained in the ‘extremely bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘high’ levels over the past day.

Buybacks On The Table

Zagury also said the company could buy back its own stock. “When our shares trade below the value of the assets attributable to them, repurchases deserve serious consideration,” he wrote, adding that any repurchase would be subject to liquidity, approvals and applicable restrictions.

No buyback has been announced. The letter lists repurchasing shares alongside buying Bitcoin, acquiring businesses and preserving liquidity as competing uses of the company’s capital.

Zagury said he did not want the company’s success to rest on predicting markets. “I would rather build one that can endure when we are wrong, take advantage of opportunities when they appear, and continue creating value through different market environments,” the CEO added.

XXI’s share price has been down over 43% so far this year and nearly 70% in the last 12 months.

data.title: Sammaan Capital Q2 Results: Profit edges up to ₹312 crore, net interest income turns negative
data.description:
Sammaan Capital, on Saturday, November 14, reported a 1.3% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit at ₹312.34 crore for the September quarter from ₹308.47 crore in the year-ago period.

However, the company’s net interest income (NII) or core income turned into a loss of ₹138.06 crore in Q2FY27, against a profit of ₹163.02 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. This is because interest costs of ₹1,299.32 crore exceeded interest income of ₹1,161.26 crore during the quarter.

On a sequential basis, net profit rose 28.4% from ₹243.30 crore in Q1 FY27. Profit before tax increased to ₹424.57 crore from ₹326.01 crore in the previous quarter, while total income rose 10% quarter-on-quarter to ₹1,850.85 crore.

Revenue from operations stood at ₹1,849.97 crore, down from ₹2,250.60 crore in Q2FY26. The year-on-year decline was partly offset by higher gains on fair value changes, which increased to ₹648.11 crore from ₹291.64 crore a year ago.

Gains on derecognition of financial instruments, meanwhile, declined sharply to ₹7.19 crore from ₹468.81 crore.

The company’s assets under management (AUM) stood at ₹59,188 crore as of September 30, up 5% from ₹56,239 crore at the end of the previous quarter. Disbursements rose 62% sequentially to ₹6,278 crore, compared with ₹3,875 crore in Q1FY27. The company disbursed around 30,700 loans during the quarter.

Asset quality improved during the quarter, with gross non-performing assets (GNPA) declining to 0.15% from 0.21% in Q1 FY27, while net non-performing assets (NNPA) fell to 0.11% from 0.15%. The company reported a blended cumulative collection efficiency of 99.6%.

Sammaan Capital’s capital adequacy ratio stood at 20%, while its net worth was ₹19,445 crore as of September 30, excluding the ₹906 crore received from the first tranche of warrant conversion completed on October 30.

The company also expanded its branch network to 245 branches across 20 states, from 217 branches in the previous quarter. It is targeting 270 branches by the end of FY27.

For the first half of FY27, consolidated profit after tax stood at ₹555.64 crore, compared with ₹642.77 crore in the year-ago period.

Shares of Sammaan Capital ended 0.2% higher at ₹137.80 on Friday, ahead of the September quarter results announcement. The stock has gained almost 4% since January this year.

data.title: 'Don't rush to replace Jensen Huang': Nvidia investors urge board to keep comeback option open
data.description:
Two prominent Nvidia investors have urged the company's board to take a measured approach to deciding its future leadership, warning against rushing to appoint a successor to Jensen Huang and asking directors to keep open the possibility of his return as chief executive.

In a letter addressed to the Nvidia board, Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital, and Gavin Baker, managing partner and chief investment officer of Atreides Management, said shareholders deserved a deliberate process as the company navigates the uncertainty surrounding Huang's departure.

Gerstner shared the letter on X on Saturday, November 14, saying it outlined the minimum standards the board owed shareholders as it managed the situation.

Brad Gerstner
@altcap

This letter was sent to the Nvidia Board today which we believe outlines the minimum acceptable standards the Board owes shareholders as it manages this difficult situation. Onward. ???? https://t.co/fIsyXVQ5tR

Nov 13, 2026

The investors said Huang's long record of leadership and the uncertainty surrounding recent events made it important for the board to avoid a rushed decision. They added that Nvidia could continue to be led by interim chief executive Colette Kress and her team while directors took time to assess the situation.

The letter also made clear that the board would retain the right to decide against bringing Huang back if, after all the facts were known, it concluded that his return was not in shareholders' best interests. However, the investors argued that the company's founder and long-time leader deserved a fair and deliberate process before being replaced.

Calls grow for Jensen Huang's return

The letter adds to growing calls from some Nvidia shareholders, employees and industry figures for Huang to return following his sudden exit.

Elon Musk had earlier backed a petition seeking Huang's reinstatement, saying he was signing it in response to a post by a Tesla Superintelligence engineer urging Nvidia employees to stand up for the company's leadership.

Separately, an internal employee suggestion-box post calling for the board to consider employee sentiment drew more than 1,600 comments, most of them supporting Huang's return, according to a Wired report. The internal post was submitted before Huang's resignation and should be distinguished from the petition Musk referred to.

Meanwhile, the Financial Times reported that Nvidia's board had approached Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas as a possible successor. Haas previously spent seven years at Nvidia, where he held senior roles, including vice president and general manager of computing products. The report said he was among several potential candidates; there was no confirmation that he had been offered the position.

Why did Jensen Huang leave Nvidia?

Nvidia announced on November 12 that Huang had stepped down as president, chief executive and board member with immediate effect. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named interim CEO, while the board began searching for a permanent successor.

The announcement followed reports about Huang's personal relationships and allegations involving Alice Huang, a Singapore-based businesswoman whom US authorities reportedly suspected of having links to Chinese intelligence. Huang has acknowledged being unfaithful, but Nvidia's official announcement did not specify a reason for his departure.

The developments had prompted scrutiny of the company's leadership and a board-level review. Nvidia said its independent directors had initiated an investigation, adding that the board had no reason to believe that US national security or the company's confidential information had been compromised. Huang has said he supports the review and is cooperating.

The board has yet to announce a permanent successor or clarify whether Huang could return to the company.

data.title: Rs.150 Dividend Alert! Record date next week of Jockey firm for biggest payout declared in Q2 - check key dates, history
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Page Industries, the listed innerwear and athleisure manufacturer, has announced its second interim dividend for FY27, making it the only company so far to declare a three-digit interim dividend during the September quarter. The company has declared a payout of Rs.150 per equity share, the largest among the interim dividends announced during Q2 FY27, with the record date scheduled for next week.

The dividend announcement comes alongside the company's September-quarter results, which showed a 4% increase in net profit. However, the stock has remained under pressure, declining 21% over the past year. Investors will therefore be tracking both the upcoming dividend record date and the company's financial performance.

The company's board of directors considered and approved the second interim dividend for FY27.

"The Board of Directors of the Company at their meeting held today (i.e., 12 November 2026) has declared the 2nd Interim Dividend for the financial year 2026-27 for an amount of Rs.150/- per equity share," read the BSE filing released earlier in the day.

The Rs.150 per-share payout is the largest interim dividend announced so far during the September quarter.

The board has fixed Wednesday, November 18, 2026, as the record date to determine shareholders' eligibility for the dividend. This effectively makes Tuesday, November 17, the last date for investors to qualify for the corporate action.

"The record date fixed for the payment of interim dividend is 18 November 2026. The date fixed for payment of dividend is on or before 11 December 2026," read the BSE filing.

The company has stated that the dividend payment will be completed on or before December 11, 2026.

Since 2024, Page Industries Ltd. has distributed Rs.1,800 per share through ten interim dividends.

In FY2024-25, the company announced four payouts aggregating Rs.900 per share. These included Rs.300 in August 2024, followed by Rs.250 in November 2024, Rs.150 in February 2025 and Rs.200 in May 2025.

For FY2025-26, Page Industries distributed another four interim dividends totalling Rs.550 per share. The company paid Rs.150 in August 2025, Rs.125 in November 2025, Rs.125 in February 2026 and Rs.150 in May 2026.

Continuing into FY2026-27, the company declared a first interim dividend of Rs.200 in August 2026 and a second interim dividend of Rs.150 in November 2026, with the record date set for November 18, 2026. This takes the dividend declared for the current financial year to Rs.350 per share so far.

Alongside Page Industries' Rs.150 payout, several major Indian companies announced notable interim dividends during the Q2 FY27 earnings season.

Sanofi India led the group with an interim dividend of Rs.75 per share, followed by IT major Infosys, which announced a payout of Rs.26 per share.

In the industrial and specialty chemicals sectors, Ingersoll-Rand India declared Rs.20 per share, while Galaxy Surfactants approved a dividend of Rs.18 per share. Great Eastern Shipping Company rounded out the notable double-digit dividend announcements with an interim payout of Rs.14.40 per share.

Stock price trend

Page Industries shares have remained under pressure in recent periods. The stock declined 13% in one week, 16% in one month and 21% over the past year.

The shares ended 2% lower at Rs.31,399.65 apiece on the BSE on Friday. The stock had touched its 52-week high of Rs.43,823.90 in July 2026 and its 52-week low of Rs.29,800 in March 2026.

Page Industries reported an 11.5% year-on-year increase in net revenue to Rs.1,439 crore during the September quarter. The Jockey licensee also recorded a 5.5% increase in sales volume.

However, profitability growth remained relatively modest amid elevated raw material costs.

The Bengaluru-based apparel manufacturer reported a 7.4% annual increase in EBITDA to Rs.300 crore, with an EBITDA margin of 20.8%. Net profit rose 4% to Rs.202.5 crore, while net total expenses increased 15% to Rs.1,131 crore.

For the first half of FY27, Page Industries reported a 9.7% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs.2,860 crore, while sales volume grew 5.6% to 121.7 million pieces.

Commenting on the results, V.S. Ganesh, Managing Director of Page Industries, said the company delivered double-digit revenue growth in Q2 FY27, supported by healthy volume growth, premiumisation and a strong consumer response to new product launches. He acknowledged that raw material costs remained elevated but said profitability had stayed within the company's planned range.

He added that positive demand trends, strong brand momentum, an encouraging pipeline of new product ranges and ongoing operational efficiency initiatives would support the company's growth outlook.

Brokerage views on Page Industries remain important for investors assessing the stock's prospects after its recent decline and the latest quarterly performance. HSBC has retained a positive view on the company, although it has reduced its target price following weaker-than-expected volume growth.

HSBC maintained its Buy rating on Page Industries but cut its target price to Rs.43,870 per share, implying an upside of approximately 40% from the previous close.

The brokerage highlighted that Page Industries' volume growth slowed to 5.5% in Q2 FY27, significantly below its estimate of 10%. However, it attributed part of the weakness to the shift in the festive calendar. Despite the earnings miss, Page Industries has retained its guidance for double-digit volume growth in FY27. HSBC said achieving this target would require volume growth of approximately 14% in the second half of the financial year.

The brokerage marginally reduced its earnings per share (EPS) estimates for FY27-FY29 by 1-3% and trimmed the valuation multiple assigned to the stock to 48 times earnings.
